meaning.R01: An invoice requires both an existing purchase order and a receipt record before automatic payment.
meaning.R02: An invoice variance of exactly EUR 10 is within tolerance.
meaning.R03: An invoice variance above EUR 10 blocks automatic payment.
meaning.R04: For a blocked invoice, an Accounts Payable analyst may ask for a corrected invoice but is not obliged to ask.
meaning.R05: Only the receiving team records goods receipt; Accounts Payable cannot record goods receipt.
meaning.R06: The person who changed supplier bank details must not approve payment to those details.
meaning.R07: For a service invoice, an authorised service acceptance replaces the goods receipt record.
meaning.R08: Service acceptance does not replace the purchase-order requirement.
meaning.R09: A dispute freezes the payment clock until the dispute is resolved.
meaning.R10: After dispute resolution, the payment clock resumes from its paused value rather than restarting at zero.
meaning.R11: An invoice number is unique only within a supplier; different suppliers may reuse the same number.
meaning.R12: The tolerance is assessed per invoice, not against the monthly sum of a supplier invoices.

forbidden_inferences.text: A service invoice with service acceptance does not need a purchase order.
An analyst must request a corrected invoice for every blocked invoice.
Resolution restarts the payment clock at zero.
An invoice can be paid automatically when no receipt record exists.
The bank-details editor may approve payment to the edited details.
Invoice numbers are globally unique across all suppliers.
A variance of exactly EUR 10 is outside tolerance.
Accounts Payable may record goods receipt.
A service invoice always needs a goods receipt even with authorised service acceptance.
A variance of EUR 11 permits automatic payment.
The payment clock continues to run during a dispute.
Apply tolerance to the monthly sum instead of each invoice.

source_scope: All 12 explicitly numbered synthetic rules. All are treated as critical controls in this internal replay; not a validated severity rubric.
